```{=html}
<div class="about-grid"><figure class="about-photo"><img src="assets/qing-han.jpg" alt="Portrait of Qing Han" width="620" height="826"><figcaption>Qing Han · 韩晴</figcaption></figure><div class="about-text"><h2>Research & practice</h2><p>I work on questions in science and technology studies through historical inquiry and anthropological methods. I am interested in how categories of personhood, value, and knowledge take shape—and how they become consequential through technologies and institutions.</p><p>I hold an MSc in Social Anthropology from the University of Oxford and a BA in Social Sciences from King’s College London. My Oxford dissertation developed the concept of <em>fantamacy</em> (fantasy intimacy) through ethnographic research on mengnü culture and Chinese otome-game fandoms.</p><p>My projects follow these questions into different settings: aging and care technologies; commercial and investment visions of the future; translation as a technology of knowledge; and changing definitions of good talent in an era of AI recruitment. Across them, I ask who gets to define a need, establish a standard, or decide what counts as evidence.</p><p>Historical inquiry helps me examine how these categories came to seem natural and how their meanings have changed. Ethnography brings me close to the decisions, relationships, and frictions through which they are sustained or contested.</p><p>I translated <a href="writing/ancient-hongshan-kingdom.html"><em>The Ancient Hongshan Kingdom</em> (红山古国)</a>, a published children’s picture book introducing Hongshan cultural heritage to English-language readers.</p><p>My work in AI product development and cultural heritage translation also gives me a situated view of these processes. I move between making practical decisions and examining the assumptions they carry, keeping the difference between professional participation and research evidence in view.</p><a class="text-link" href="cv.html">View my CV <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a><div class="contact-block"><p class="eyebrow">Contact</p><a href="mailto:qinghan.research@gmail.com">qinghan.research@gmail.com</a></div></div></div><section class="interests"><p class="eyebrow">Intellectual interests</p><div class="interest-tags"><span>Historical anthropology of technology</span><span>Science & technology studies</span><span>Markets, finance & valuation</span><span>Aging & care</span><span>Intimacy & digital culture</span><span>Classification, work & AI</span><span>Cultural heritage</span></div></section>
```
